The test image shows a corn field scene with a person examining a plant. I can observe:
- Brown/tan discoloration on lower leaves and husks
- The person appears to be pulling back husks to examine an ear
- Lower plant portion shows significant browning/dying of leaves and husks
- Upper canopy still green

This suggests either an ear rot or stalk rot. The brown husks sticking to the ear and the tan coloration point toward Diplodia. Let me check the reference.

The reference images for Ear_rots_Diplodia show tan/brown papery husks clinging to the ear with white-gray mold on kernels — matching the test image where:
- Brown, papery, dried husks are visible
- The person is pulling back husks to inspect the ear
- Lower leaves show characteristic browning/dying associated with a diseased ear
- Overall plant browning from lower portion upward

This pattern is consistent with Diplodia ear rot, which causes tan-brown husks that adhere tightly to the ear.
